Unfortunately as it stands this is not yet a game. This is a play test, and it is not in shape to be played properly yet. The game is poorly optimised, the randomization means you may just start in a spot where there's not enough food and water to even get going, and the map is rather non-explanatory. With som balancing, more features, and added functionality this can be a lovely single player survival game. It isn't there yet. It's like playing a pre-beta release, not just "Early Access".

Early access reviews that praise a game's "potential" are kinda pointless but in this case you can clearly see where the game is heading and how good it will be when it gets there. On release it's still very bare-bones but once they've added some of the things promised on the Roadmap (notably fuel and electricity management) it *should* be an excellent "you vs. Mother Nature" survival game. If you have a realistic understanding of how early access works and are willing to contribute to the game's development (not just complain) and you're looking for an immersive real-world survival game (similar to The Long Dark, Green Hell and Survival: Fountain of Youth) you should enjoy being a part of this game's development.

So the game is barebones, missing a lot, and objectively: an unfinished, unpolished tech demo. But I see the potential and future of this "game" that I deeply enjoy playing it. Some of the things I have to test in order to enjoy these little things because they make sense in the real world. If you wear a waterproof jacket, your insulated underwear won't get wet by the rain. the sun rises in the east, sets in the west. Lighters have fluid that can run out. insulated shoes are nice, waterproof shoes keep your feet dry. taking off clothes and getting in water won't get your clothes wet. These all make sense in hindsight, but to test them by hand it grants a sense of genuine accomplishment because no one told me or explained to me how this works. I was dying of hypothermia, My matches were completely soaked. I found a cabin and there were no matches. I thought outside the box. turned on the generator to the home. swapped some fuses to turn off the lights, but I turned on the stove. throw all my firewood on the lit stovetops. they're burning. it saved my life. No one told me I could do this, it just makes sense. If there's going to be more types of interactivity of this base level and beyond, I look forward to its future.

Far too many bugs. As it is now, it's barely playable. I spent many enjoyable hours with the game, which is why I bought it when it was released in early access. But since early access, I haven't been able to complete a single playthrough. Items that you drop fall through the floor, never to be seen again, the little green dot in the middle of the screen for clicking on things doesn't do what it's supposed to, items can't be selected, and today I died of thirst standing in the middle of a river because the option to drink was gone... It's such a shame. I'll come back once the game has received some updates.

I know the reviews are mixed, and a lot of you are complaining that the game is missing tons of elements. I won't disagree—it's still unfinished, lacking features, content, goals, items, mechanics, and more. BUT, I remember starting during the playtest and beta. I was totally lost, digging online just to figure out how to play. Graphics were rough: rocks looked awful, no food or water in the starting cabin, weird weather mechanics, and a horrible landscape. Despite all that, I sunk over 30 hours into that beta! I've watched it transform: Food, water, and lighting options added to the starting cabin. Graphics overhauled—rocks now look realistic! Bugs fixed (no more getting trapped in rocks or trees after we reported them). Landscapes turning stunning with each update. Yes, it's Early Access, so expect it to be a work in progress. But this steady evolution makes it worth playing now and worth the wait. It's a fresh take on the genre that will surprise and delight you as it grows. The devs were super responsive during playtest and beta—active on Discord, reading every comment and suggestion and this is the reason I was more than happy to buy the game in EA to support the team who develop this game, because supporting them will allow me to eventually enjoy the end result. Yes you will die more often than you succeed, but dont let that discouraged you. This unique gem is on track to become a masterpiece!

Although I actually like this game, I have to downvote because I do not recommend it to anyone. Accept a loser mindset because you will die 99.9% of your runs, especially if you don't know how to read a topographical map. This game is brutally hard and unrewarding. it's confusing because it wants to take itself seriously and wants to be immersive but immersion is constantly broken with insane weather patterns, time being on super fast forward and most of your time somehow in the pitch black dark. Peaceful daylight hours are rare and fleeting, along with your water and food intake being absurd. All of these systems are so broken that you have to use unrealistic gamer instincts to over come most challenges. The maps are highly unrealistic with random cabins thrown about in unrealistic gamer patterns once you understand how it works. This is not a chill game. its a sprint to the finish across an extremely hard to get across terrain. My only real complaint is that the primary survival mechanics are far too unrealistic when it's trying to be. The only way to actually survive is to play like a gamer and not think realistically. Also, the only update so far has been in the wrong direction for immersion. They seem to be focused on electrical power systems to cabins that realistically you shouldn't spend more than 5mins at. Not the one forgiving system, which was finding working stoves is going to be far harder to come by. The stoves are actually such an absolute key to basic survival that it's comically unrealistic even further. This game has a lot of development to go through for just being a passion project. As of right now it's just an arcade running survival simulator racing game. It's different than likely anything you've ever played, do not come into it with expectations.

GAME IS ABANDONED. IT WAS A CASH GRAB SCAM. (06/12/26) Do I recommend this "game?" I don't think the term "game" describes it accurately. Poker is a game, Connect Four is a game, The Long Dark is a game. This is not a game and therefore I cannot recommend it. This doesn't mean I have not enjoyed my time playing it. This "game" feels more like a graphics tech demo than a "game." A "game" means there are mechanics and rules that are intuitive and mechanics that are articulated so the "players" can engage in the "game." Currently, this feels like a janky, unoptimized, open world that occasionally you can interact with in a limited manner that makes little sense. This game's version of survival is more convoluted and unintuitive than actually surviving in real life. I cannot even figure out how to throw a match in this game to light a fire. Half the time my character will miss the kindling, the other half of the time the match immediately disappears. In real life, I can just get a match, lighter, or a torch and hold it underneath a tumbleweed, firestarter, newspaper, or a cotton ball... and I have fire. It's not hard. I can make a fire in real life easier than this game LOL. Be aware of that. I have played it a little, I like the idea of the game and I want to play it again when it has more time to cook. Currently, this game is raw and needs to go back in the oven for probably 2 more years. I don't see this being feature complete, optimized, bug free, and intuitively designed until late 2027 or early 2028. I am not going to return this, because I want to support what this game can eventually become.

So i did a run and it was pretty easy but also quite boring. Get map and compass, look where you need to go, aim in the direction, keep running that direction no matter what, rain, storm, heat, cold, doesnt matter, get to the goal, but fail because you need to climb a rock but end up climbing into it and get stuck. The trailer suggests its a game about crafting survival stuff, preparing, equipping and foraging, but i spent 2 hours running through a forest, looting huts that had nothing into them other than some wood and occasional food. Because my only matchsticks to light a fire soaked wet directly at the start going out the door and having no way to change that, i used the oven to light sticks on fire but couldnt carry them to the fireplace, so every hut i came across got burned down because i stacked wood on the oven to dry my clothes. Occasionally they got burned too. It was also pointless, because my 2 hours consistet of only rain, storm and rainy night and heavy rain, so i was constantly wet the moment i stepped out of a door. Which meant i tried taking care of that the first hour and then didnt care any further and just ran to the goal. The logical content addition would be clothes or equipment thats heavily resistent to rain, but that somehow was too complicated for the devs to add. Also dealing with staying dry is objectively pointless, because even IF i somehow managed to do that, the game seems to ever generate a river on every map you start and you need to swim through it, which, gets you and your clothes soaked again. The game didnt seem to give any reason to care about these things, so why would i. At least i didnt feel any consequences in terms of gameplay. Trailer suggests open fields and such, nope. I had only rock formations, mountains packed with forest, so i could maybe see 30 metres straight. Found a looking glass that turned out pointless because of this. Maybe map generation scammed me, but i wont give that another try without coop. The cardinal sin here is the lack of coop AND the "meh" graphics mixed with bad optimization. However if this had coop, i could look past a few issues and treat this as a PEAK but realistic version. And i think the lack of coop is what killed it for most. As otherwise i would see a lot of people enjoying exploration, survival hiking and the challenge but with friends. Getting lost and finding each other again on the journey. Pack in a few interesting locations and hideouts, add some danger stuff and then build the ambience with some wildlife (i have not seen any animal) and profit. Could have been cool, but was overfunded without any logical base features like coop. Seems like a proof of concept title, which is kind of sad.

I played this 'Game' so you don't have to. Or maybe you should, just to see a fantastic example of everything wrong with systems based games. They are not fun, they are frustration simulators. It's not just this game, it's all games that think realism is a good idea, then fail to implement realism. Sometimes it will rain for days at a time, no problem, I'll just drop this bucket in the rain and catch some water to boil on the stove. Oh no, it doesn't collect water. But I can drink from the puddle of mud that's formed below the bucket, oh now I've got some poisoning from drinking the water and I've died of starvation because of it. If you are going for realism you have to implement actual working mechanics players could use to survive in the real world, if not, then it's not realism it's a torture simulator. Good job the devs abandoned this terrible idea for a game.

Amazing game conception! Not bad survival game! This game was inspired by DayZ. PROS: - Game has very interesting conception. AI-ML generative world, but with special AI that was learned by many-many real NASA photos to generate more realistic game world. - Game has huge potential, but it's still need many improvements, and some bugfixing. - This game is really about surviving. - Even with all CONS game feels smooth. - You can setup you custom world and tweak world settings. - Game will have continue in another title. CONS: - Developing is stopped for unknown time. Team that worked on this game are gone, and no one now working on it... - The physics of the world is sometimes absurd, so sometimes it is impossible to light a fire where in reality it would light very easily. - In normal mode, houses are literally blown to pieces by the wind, but before you came to that house, it was as if it was standing and waiting to begin to crumble above your head. - In-game Time goes by very, very quickly. - No in-world animals. - There are not enough ways to interact with the world to survive. - Game is very short and empty, and require more content and physics fixing to be enough fun.

So, we all hate for the indies to fail at their game. However, what a grand failure this is. Are there some bugs... a few, but the game is in a somewhat finished state now. I got it free after seeing it was not going to make it and the company was going to stop. They added lots of nice features at the end and I really hope the mod community will step up and keep this going. It is easily the most brutal survival game I've played. Easiest ways to die are freezing to death, falling from too high, dehydration, and starvation. You can learn ways to get cope with these, but the BEST part is there is NO minimap and you must dead recon using a compass, a map, and a pace counter (I think one step = 1 meter). IF you enjoy a real nailbiting challenge of a survival game, you can't go wrong with free. I have yet to survive, but I am using the custom settings to get through a single MAP of the billions they have (used map data to create them all... no repeats unless you want it). I really think if you enjoy a struggle to survive, this one offers unique challenges and now this nearly commercial game quality is FREE.... High recommend as it is fun, hard, and free. update: Can't stop playing it. Still my current game I'm playing. What I think it would be GREAT with is if it had a story that you built up over time. Would love a reply if anyone is modding and could tell me where to go and try to help create a compelling story OVER time and over several runs. Why is this place abandoned? Why do you "awaken" and have the same crappy clothes and then need to run to the tower again. What are the 6 slot batteries for and what is on the red floppy disks. What if you could read your floppies at the radio tower and they filled in the blanks till you got to an eventual "boss level" map once you checked all the boxes and found all the lore. I'd want to play over and over till I got the full lore. My mind keeps wanting to fill in WHY are we constantly having to run to the tower over and over and seem to have amnesia... AND WHY are there no animals or people or even bones. Would LOVE to be on a team that is trying to make this happen. Just reply to my comment and send a link in the comment for where there might be a mod community...

Hear me out- the whole idea of the game is PERFECT. I love the fact that is difficult and challenging but it is really poorly done. No matter what settings I set on EPIC, the Compass will still be blurry, so I have finished the game after so many hours playing it blindly, finding a route where I'd think I should go. The compass and map are the only things needed to finish the game and one of them is not working properly. Let me walk you through the bugs and reasons why I have died several times and had to start the game all over again: - I went a long way, hungry as hell with no cabin/house in sight. After a long walk I finally found a cabin/house and in the fridge I found 2 packages of pasta (that requires water and a cooking pot to be boiled on the stove) which I all had. In the matter of minutes I had left before dying of hunger, I took my cooking pot out of my backpack filled with water to put it on the floor so that I could add pasta and put it on the stove to boil- the cooking pot went through the floor (not below the house but in the wood). I panicked, went outside and guess what - it was the only house I found that you were unable to duck below it. I could see the pot 'hanging' from the floor but I just couldn't reach it. Tried to find another pot but no luck and eventually I died because eating 2 packages of raw pasta gives you almost nothing to satisfy your hunger. - You know how some houses have bathrooms in it and a bath tub, well once I was looting for food, accidentally went into the bath tub and couldn't get out and died. Tried the 'Unstuck' button and it didn't help. - Wheat looking thing on the fields are probably the only thing beside spoiled food that you can't eat (and drink water from the ground). So there I was, eating wild carrots and whatsnot when I took a bite of that wheat looking thing and it made me sick (eating more of them didn't help, don't ask me how I know that) so eventually I died, again. That was the time that I thought once you get sick you die, but all you have to do is find another food (lots of it) and eat all the time while the sickness passes. About me falling down the regular and final tower I won't waste words, being stuck in between two mountains also, being stuck in a mud as well, etc. There are many bugs in the game and I am sad that developers decided not to fix them and stop working on the game. Things like if you drop an item (for example a flashlight) on the doorstep, you will be unable to retrieve it because the interaction box is only for the door. Cooking pot going through the floor as previously explained. Houses/shelters/cabins blending with the trees, blurry compass, lack of the loot, fire going out in the fireplace because its raining outside. The grey, literally unclimbable mountains that surrounds, well basically everything is such an annoying thing. I tried hundreds ways and parts of the mountains/wall to climb over it so that I could get closer to the weather tower but unlucky. Last night I finally found a way to climb onto one and guess what - it was pointless. No way to go from there and believe me, I've tried. Finally, I found a 'gap' between these wall looking mountains and continued the road to the weather tower. Sadly, I do not recommend this game even tho I loved the concept of the game so much. Very laggy/buggy, many bugs, unfortunate events, once you die you start the game from the beginning while the entire map and ground/river/tower/cabins shifts to a whole new way which is good- you can't remember the path but lack of food mostly is the main cause of deaths.

It's a shame the developers had to stop this project, but in this market it is easily understandable. For my part, I'm sorry my times are hard and I couldn't financially support it. It is really painful to admit to this, especially since exploration is a genre I deeply appreciate. The game, in its current production state (I didn't try the developer branch) is almost ready imho, to get out of EA and ask for a fair price, around 10€ or 15€. I find that this would be a good price given the challenge and the re-playability. That being said, the things that are lacking in game are some QoL and polishing, like a "real" tutorial with an NPC to give directions and/or fall damage and injuries and broken limbs management. Also stamina management. I still had a very nice time playing this, the quietness of a hike in the mountains mixed with the challenge of survival felt so refreshing. I'd very much appreciate to see this project revived or a sequel with aforementioned improvements and multiplayer. Thank you devs for bringing this experience to life and especially for the decision to make it free in these dire times.

If anything, they should make a version of this where you just maintain your own cabin, survive and maybe have a little garden for planting. At it's current being free I'd recommend it, however if the full game comes out in this same state at any price over 10, then I would not.
